# The built add-in, in the repository

`Bench-<version>.g3a` is the add-in exactly as CI built it. It lives here so the
calculator's file is in the repository itself, not only behind a release page, a
workflow artifact or blob storage that some networks cannot reach.

`BUILD.txt` beside it is generated by the build and says which version, which
commit, which day, the size and the SHA-256. Trust that file over this one if
they ever disagree.

## Which copy is which

| Where | What it is |
|---|---|
| `dist/` | a snapshot of one green build, with `BUILD.txt` recording exactly which |
| `builds` branch | the same file, force-pushed on every build: `git fetch origin builds` |
| releases | `v<version>` is the released build; `auto` is replaced every few days |
| `bench-g3a` artifact | each CI run's output: `Bench-<version>.g3a` |
| `bench-spike` artifact | the M1 diagnostic add-in, separate on purpose (see `docs/spike.md`) |

CI refreshes this folder for tagged builds and automatic builds, as a commit
marked `[skip ci]`, so the copy cannot drift far. If it and a release disagree,
the release is the one to trust: it carries the same bytes as the `builds`
branch at the time of the build.

## Installing

Copy the `.g3a` to the calculator over USB (Flash mode), then run **Bench** from
the main menu. `version.txt` names the file, so the file, the About screen and
the tag always agree.

Verified on hardware? Not this build. The screens and the maths are tested on a
PC (`make test`, `make check-screens`), the sources are compiled against the
real gint headers in CI, but nobody has run this particular `.g3a` on a
calculator.
